- **`git worktree prune`** (remove of a directory that is already gone) drops git's record of every stale worktree of
  that repository, not only this ticket's; other registrations whose directory is gone then fail closed (gitdir
  mismatch) until removed.
- **Not built:** `worktree.in_use` is only as good as the runner's run records (a run started outside the host is not
  seen); there is no addon check in direct mode.

### 12.8 Records commit and push (#308) [SC]

**What records are:** `events/workspace.jsonl`, `keys.jsonl`, `config.json`, `AGENTS.orch.md`, and per ticket
`ticket.json`, `body.md`, `events.jsonl`, `artifacts/*`; never `.state/` or `addons/`. Git metadata (trailer, author)
is transport metadata, never authorization or freshness: consumers verify by F1 replay and checkpoints, and
`AGENTS.orch.md` and `config.json` get no authority from sitting in the repo.

```
records.status   {current_url?:str} → {configured:bool, repo:{state:"ok"|"missing"|"not_dedicated"|"unsafe"|
                       "index_differs", problem?:str} | null, pending:{events:int, tickets:[{key:Key, events:int}]
                       {0..200}, more:bool, workspace_events:int}, last:{commit:Sha, at:Time, by:Person, ws_seq:int,
                       pushed_at:Time | null} | null, auto:{on:bool, every_min:int, push:bool} | null,
                       remote:{url:str | null, private:bool, export:"ok"|"blocked_convenience",
                       current_url:str | null, current_private:bool | null, matches_last:bool | null} | null}
                       // remote: the push URL git resolves now (§12.8), shown through visible.tsx
                       // configured: the workspace's records repo exists (#441 follow-up; see "As built")
records.snapshot {page?:str} → {manifest:Hash, ws_seq:int, heads:{str:Hash}, taken_at:Time,
                       files:[{path:str, size:int, sha256:Hash}]{0..2000}, next_page:str | null}
records.export_check {sha:Sha, url:str{1..512}, ref:str, history_convenience:bool} → {ok:true}
records.note     {manifest:Hash, commit:Sha, pushed:bool, url?:str} → {}
```

- `manifest` = digest over (workspace id, `ws_seq`, chain heads, file list); pages belong to it and expire after
  10 min. The host may cache file hashes by (path, size, inode, mtime) so the store lock is not held for re-hashing
  immutable artifacts. `pending.tickets` lists only visible tickets; counts are aggregates.
- **Commit:** a dedicated repo only (the record root is its top level; `orch records init` creates it), else
  `records.not_dedicated`; no `MERGE_HEAD`, `REBASE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` or detached `HEAD`
  (`records.git_state`). Local and worktree config (includes counted) may not set `url`, `http`, `credential`,
  `protocol`, `filter`, `core.sshCommand`, `core.askPass`, `core.gitProxy`, `core.fsmonitor`, a foreign
  `core.hooksPath`, or anything for the remote in use but `url`, `fetch` and #254's harmless keys; one URL per remote
  (`records.unsafe_config` names the key). Each path is resolved component-wise under the record root fd with
  `O_NOFOLLOW` (regular files only), read **once**, exactly `size` bytes, hashed, and those bytes go to `git
  hash-object -w --stdin`; 64 MiB per file, 1 GiB per snapshot (`records.too_large`); a mismatch retries the snapshot
  once (`records.snapshot_changed`). `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp>`, `git read-tree --empty`, add exactly the manifest,
  `write-tree`, `ls-tree -r` must equal the manifest, `commit-tree -p HEAD` (message `orch: records <PREFIX> ws_seq
  <n>`, trailer `Orch-Records: <workspace id>`, author and committer `orch records <records@orch.invalid>`),
  `update-ref` compare-and-swap. The real index is refreshed only if it equalled the old `HEAD^{tree}`; otherwise
  `records.status` says "index differs, run `orch records sync-index`". The working tree is never written.
- **History:** at `orch records init` on an existing repo, or before the first push, every commit reachable from the
  branch must be a records commit of this workspace with a records-only tree, else the tool refuses and offers a fresh
  orphan history. The validated tip is kept in `records.json`; later pushes validate `tip..HEAD`.
  `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`; `info/grafts` and shallow repos are refused.
- **Push:** fast-forward only. The tool resolves the effective push URL once (`pushurl`, else `url`; `insteadOf` and
  `pushInsteadOf` already refused), validates the history, scans the event logs reachable from S for an event with
  `auth:"convenience"` (#441, see "Push rule"), calls `records.export_check` with that literal URL and the scan's report, all before any
  network call, then `ls-remote`s it, checks that the
  remote tip T is an ancestor of the commit S, and runs `git -c push.followTags=false push --no-recurse-submodules
  --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:T <url> S:refs/heads/<b>`. A missing remote branch only with `orch records push
  --initial` (terminal). Divergence or a lease failure: `records.push_rejected`, never a rebase.
- **Every git call:** argv only, `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false`, environment `{HOME, PATH,
  SSH_AUTH_SOCK, LANG=C, LC_ALL=C, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=https:ssh, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1}`,
  `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` unless a global `core.sshCommand`, stdin closed, 10 s local, 20 s network, 60 s per run.
  System and global config are the person's and are read.
- **Who:** owners and maintainers (a push exports every ticket, restricted ones included; the UI says so). Agents get
  `op.not_allowed` (`records.snapshot` is P only).
- **Starting it:** `orch records commit|push|status|init|sync-index`, the dashboard server as a fixed-argv child
  (`python -I -m orch.records commit [--push] --workspace <id> --json`; it reads the root from the person's own
  registry), or the timer unit `io.orch.records` / `orch-records.timer` every 5 min for auto mode. One run per
  workspace at a time (a lock in the person state dir).
- **Local config** `<person state>/records.json` (0600): per workspace `{auto, every_min:5..1440, push,
  private_remotes:[url], validated_tip}`. `orch records auto on|off [--push] [--every N]` and `orch records remote
  private URL` are terminal only; the dashboard may switch `auto` off, never on. **The private mark is the URL git
  itself resolves for the push** (`git remote get-url --push <remote>`, after `insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf` are refused):
  that exact string is stored and later compared byte for byte with the URL git resolves at push time; no other
  normalization (case, trailing `/` or `.git`) is applied, so any change of the URL needs a new mark. **Private remote (owner decision,
  12 Oct 2026):** the terminal prompt and the Records page say "orch trusts your word that only you read <url>".
- **Log:** `<person state>/person/records.jsonl` (0600, 1 MiB × 4): start, commit, push result, refusal codes; never
  contents or credentials. #309's hook installer never touches the records repo.

#### As built in H11e (#430 and part 2)

Where this differs from the text above, the code follows the tie-break (D-P2-33 Codex in full, D-P2-34) and the owner
decision of 12 Oct 2026 on the private remote; this list is what is built.

- **Cap and ops.** `records/1` with `records.snapshot`, `records.export_check`, `records.status` (reads, op kind
  `person_read`: column P, owner or maintainer) and `records.remote_private`, `records.note` (writes, op kind
  `person_write`, column P only: `opts.idem` required, no `dry_run`, an outcome record, a retry replays it).
  `records.remote_private` is for **owners only**. G and N get `op.not_allowed`.
  - `records.snapshot {page?}` → `{workspace, manifest, ws_seq, heads, taken_at, count, bytes, files, next_page}`
    (no `for` argument; the export decision is `records.export_check`).
  - `records.export_check {sha, url, ref, history_convenience}` → `{workspace, sha, url, ref, history_convenience,
    policy:"none"|"private_remote", convenience, check}` or `sign.convenience_readers`; it takes no `manifest` (the
    push may be of an older commit). `history_convenience` (required, #441) is the tool's report that an event log
    reachable from `sha` holds an event with top-level `auth:"convenience"`; `convenience` is true when the flag is
    on, the durable `convenience_seen` mark is set, the merged history (or a cut tail) holds such an event, or the
    report says so. A merged-history or cut-tail hit sets the mark; **the report never does**: it refuses this push
    only.
  - `records.remote_private {url?, on}` → `{private_remote:{url, at, by} | null, text}`.
  - `records.note {manifest?, commit?, pushed, url?, repo?:{state, problem?}, auto?}` → `{}`; a `manifest` must be
    one this caller took and the host still holds (`page.expired` otherwise). Notes are kept **per person**
    (`lasts[<person>]`, at most 64), with `last_noted {by, at}` workspace-wide (#433 review, Opus finding 1).
  - `records.status {current_url?}` → as in the block above, for **the caller's own** last note (another manager's
    note never changes it), plus `last_noted`. `repo` and `remote.url` come from the caller's last commit or push
    note (the host runs no git, D-P2-19). `remote.url` is **display only**: a client never passes it to
    `records.remote_private` (the tool resolves the URL to mark from git itself). The tool's `status` adds `local
    {repo, url}` as it sees them now and writes nothing.
  - **`configured`** means **the workspace's records repo exists** (not "a note exists"): the last repo state any
    tool reported for the workspace (`repo {state, at, by}` in the host's `records.json`, from any manager's note;
    a record from before it falls back to any person's last report) is `ok`, `index_differs` or `unsafe` (`missing`
    and `not_dedicated` are false). `orch records init` reports the repo. The tool's own `status` replaces it with
    what it sees now (`local.repo`). Same in host and direct mode.
  - **The current push URL** (for the dashboard's push confirmation): the tool's `status` passes the effective push
    URL it resolved now as `current_url` (refused like any URL that can hide a secret). The answer's `remote` then
    has `current_url` (for display: userinfo stripped; for anyone but an owner only the host, `local` for a path or
    `file://`), `current_private` (that exact string carries the private-remote mark) and `matches_last` (it equals
    the caller's last pushed destination, `remote.url`). Without `current_url` the three are `null`; `remote` is
    `null` only when there is neither a last URL nor a current one (`url` is then `null` when only the current is
    known, and `private`/`export` describe the current URL). Display only: the push resolves the URL and asks
    `records.export_check` again at push time.
- **Limits.** 64 MiB per file, 1 GiB and 200 000 files per snapshot (`records.too_large`); pages of 2 000 files bound
  to the manifest and the caller's principal for 10 min, at most 4 manifests per workspace; 50 export and 50 mark
  audit entries; `pending.tickets` at most 200. Hash cache by (path, size, inode, mtime, ctime).
- **Manifest id v1.** `m_` + SHA-256 over the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, ASCII) of `{"v":1,
  "workspace":<id>, "ws_seq":<n>, "heads":{log: head}, "files":[[path, size, sha256], …] sorted by path}`. The tool
  recomputes it from the pages.
- **Two state files.** The host's `<state>/hosts/<ws>/records.json` (0600): `private_remote` (the one mark),
  `marks` (audit: action, redacted URL, person, time), `exports` (audit of every export check), `last` (the note).
  The host's `<state>/hosts/<ws>/convenience_seen.json` (0600, #441): the durable mark (§0.8.6 item 1), never
  cleared. The host's `records.json` also keeps `repo` (the workspace's last reported repo state, for `configured`).
  The person's `<state>/records.json` (0600): `validated` (per workspace and branch, the last validated tip), `clean`
  (per workspace and branch, the last tip scanned clean of convenience events) and
  `auto` (per workspace `{on, every_min, push, root?, last_run?}`; `root` only for a direct-mode workspace,
  `last_run` the timer's own clock). In tier A both live
  in the same state directory. The mark is in the host file, not in the person's (`private_remotes:[url]` above is
  not built): one exact URL per workspace, set through a P op.
- **Tool flow** (`python -I -m orch.records`, also `orch records`). Resolve the workspace (host mode when the person's
  registry names it, else direct mode); one run per workspace (`<state>/person/records-<ws>.lock`, `records.busy`);
  60 s for the whole run, git and host calls together (`records.budget`). Commit: dedicated repo and branch checks,
  the local config deny-list, every page of `records.snapshot` (id recomputed), each file read once beneath the root
  fd with `O_NOFOLLOW` and streamed into one `git fast-import` as it is checked (one file in memory at a time),
  `read-tree --empty` into a private temporary index, `ls-tree -r` must equal the manifest, `commit-tree
  --no-gpg-sign` with the message `orch: records ws_seq <n>` + `Orch-Manifest: <id>` + `Orch-Records: <ws>`, author
  and committer `orch records <records@orch.invalid>`, `update-ref` compare-and-swap, the real index refreshed only by
  compare-and-swap (under `index.lock`, beneath the git-dir fd) when it equalled the old HEAD tree, then
  `records.note`. The commit message has no `<PREFIX>` (the trailer names the workspace).
- **History rule.** Every commit reachable from S and not from the validated tip: at most one parent, only
  `tree`/`parent`/`author`/`committer` headers, exactly the message shape above, and changes to record paths only, as
  mode 100644 (`records.not_records_only`, `records.history_invalid`). `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`,
  `core.commitGraph=false`; grafts and shallow repos refused. `commit --fresh-history` makes a root commit.
- **Push rule.** S resolved once; the effective push URL resolved once by git (`remote get-url --push`, exactly one,
  https or ssh only, no userinfo, query or fragment); `ls-remote` and `push` run in a throwaway config-free bare repo
  whose alternates name the records repo's objects, keeping only `credential.*`, `http.*`, `ssh.*` and
  `core.sshCommand` of the person's frozen system and global config (no `url.*`, no `remote.*`); any `remote.<x>.*`
  in the records repo's own config other than the remote in use is refused. **Before any network call** (#441): the
  history check, the convenience scan and `records.export_check(S, URL, ref, history_convenience)`. Then T from
  `ls-remote` must exist locally and be an ancestor of S (an up-to-date remote ends the run here), a recheck of the
  local config and the URL, and `git push --no-verify --porcelain --no-recurse-submodules --no-follow-tags
  --force-with-lease=<ref>:<T> <url> <S>:<ref>`.
- **The convenience scan** (#441, #454 review). Only event logs count: blobs at `events/workspace.jsonl` or
  `tickets/<ulid>/events.jsonl` that a commit reachable from S (and not from the tip last scanned clean) added or
  changed (`diff-tree`; the history is linear). Bodies and artifacts are free text agents write and are never read.
  A line counts when it parses as JSON, leniently (`\u` escapes, duplicate keys, any order or spacing), with
  top-level `auth` `"convenience"`; a line that does not parse as a JSON object counts too (fail closed: agents cannot
  write raw event-log lines); any parse error, `RecursionError` included, is caught. Every records git call runs with
  `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, so a partial clone never fetches behind the scan; as a backstop for git older than 2.45, a
  records repo whose own config sets `extensions.partialClone` or `remote.*.promisor`/`partialclonefilter` is
  `records.unsafe_config`. A tip scanned clean is kept as `clean
  {sha, scanner}` per workspace and branch in the person's `records.json`; an entry of another scanner version means
  a full rescan. Never a non-fast-forward. A missing remote branch needs
  `push --initial` (terminal). **The mark binds that URL string; the person's own settings (ssh config, credential
  helpers, DNS) decide how it is reached.**
- **Codes and exits** (`orch.records.RecordsError`; the host op passes the same code and exit):
  `records.snapshot_changed` 9 (retryable), `records.busy` 9, `records.budget` 9, `records.snapshot_invalid` 5,
  `records.invalid` 5, `records.timer_failed` 1, and 3 for `records.timer_conflict`, `records.not_dedicated`, `records.git_state`,
  `records.unsafe_config`, `records.not_records_only`, `records.history_invalid`, `records.tree_mismatch`,
  `records.too_large`, `records.unsafe_tree`, `records.push_rejected`, `records.remote_invalid`,
  `records.remote_missing`, `records.git_failed`, `records.unsupported` (Windows and other unsupported setups; the
  `unsupported.platform` row of §0.6 is not used), `records.unconfirmed`.
- **CLI synopsis.**
  ```
  orch records init|commit [--push] [--fresh-history]|push [--initial [--yes]]|status|sync-index
               |remote-private [--off] [--yes]|auto on [--push] [--every MIN] [--dev]|auto off|auto [--state DIR]
               [--workspace ID] [--remote NAME] [--json]
  ```
  Terminal only (asked on `/dev/tty`): `auto on`, `push --initial` and `remote-private` (the last two skip the
  question with `--yes`: the boundary is the host op, an owner-only write; the question is UX). The time spent at a
  question does not count against the 60 s budget (it restarts after the answer). `--state` is the timer's own
  option (`auto` without a switch); anywhere else it is `records.invalid`. Agents (`ORCH_GRANT`) get
  `op.not_allowed`.
- **Dashboard child.** `python -I -m orch.records commit [--push] --workspace <id> --json` and `… auto off
  --workspace <id> --json` print exactly one JSON line valid against `orch.records.cli.CHILD_SCHEMA`:
  `{ok:true, commit?, pushed?, url?, detail?}` or `{ok:false, code, message, hint?, commit?}` (`commit` when a push
  failed after the commit landed); exit 0 or the code's exit. A third argv reads the status:
  `python -I -m orch.records status --workspace <id> --json` resolves the effective push URL as a push does, calls
  `records.status {current_url}` and prints `{ok:true, detail:{status}}` (the host's answer with `local` and
  `configured` as the tool sees them now, and `remote.current_url`, `current_private`, `matches_last`). What it does
  exactly: **no writes to the records repo and no network** (`ls-remote --get-url` only, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`; the
  index is compared with `diff-index --cached`, never `write-tree`), no records lock file and no run log, and a
  throwaway temporary transport directory (the one push uses to check the literal URL). It **may record the
  convenience mark** (when the host's scan of the merged history or cut tails finds a convenience event: a host
  observation, as for any `records.status`), and in direct mode it opens the store, which takes the store lock and
  may run its recovery, like any direct-mode read. Same gitsafe and
  environment rules as push (`HOME`, `PATH`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` at most); it fits the dashboard's bounded child (60 s,
  minimal environment, `python -I`).
- **Auto mode and timer.** `auto on` asks on the terminal, writes the person's `auto` entry and installs a per-user
  timer: LaunchAgent `io.orch.records` (`StartInterval` 300) or systemd user units `orch-records.service`
  (`Type=oneshot`) and `orch-records.timer` (every 5 min), running `python -I -m orch.records auto --state <state>
  --json`. A source checkout is refused as the timer's program unless `--dev`. `auto off` removes the entry and,
  when no workspace is left, the timer, and only a timer installed for this state dir. An installed timer that
  differs (state dir, interpreter, dev versus release) is never replaced silently: `records.timer_conflict` names
  the fields, `auto on --replace` overrides (H7 parity). The timer's run decides on its own clock only (`last_run`
  in the person's file, never a host note): a due workspace is committed (a no-op when nothing changed) and pushed
  when `push` is on; one failing workspace never stops the others, and the run answers `ok:false` with the first
  code when any failed. It rotates `records-timer.log` (launchd's stdout) like the person log. Same fences as H7: the default
  runner refuses `launchctl`/`systemctl` under pytest or `ORCH_NO_SERVICE_MANAGER=1`, the test session guard refuses
  units under the real home and checks the real unit paths are unchanged.
- **Direct mode** (D-P2-38). A workspace not in the person's registry: the tool opens the store read-only under
  `DirectGuard` and runs the same ops on the same files (`host.required` once a host serves it). The host writes
  `<root>/.state/host-served` (content `{"v":1}`, created exclusively) when it starts serving a workspace and
  removes it at unregister; direct mode refuses
  while it exists, whatever state directory the tool was given. POSIX only. No role check in direct mode (the person
  owns the files; audit entries name `direct:<uid>`); the export check still applies.
- **Person log.** `<state>/person/records.jsonl` (0600, rotated at 1 MiB, 4 files): `start`, the command's result
  (commit, pushed, redacted URL), `refused` with the code; never file contents or credentials.
- **Not built.** Hashing outside the store lock (the cache bounds re-hashing; a first snapshot of a large workspace
  still hashes under the lock); validating history at `orch records init` (it runs before the first push instead).

### 12.9 Quick tasks (#308)

**Built in H11f (#429):** "As built in H11f" (§0.8) is authoritative where it differs from the design text below.

`quick.list {status?:[Status], limits?:{commits:int 1..100, files:int 1..1000}, limit?:int 1..200 = 100, page?:str}` →
`{rows:[Row & {quick:{commits:int | null, files:int | null, over:bool | null}}], next_page, total}`: exactly
`ticket.query {label:["quick"]}` for the viewer, plus per row with a linked repo and branch the counts from the host
reader (`null` when unreadable). Adding is `new` (`type: chore`) plus a label `set` (an agent: `orch quick add "…"`;
a person: two click signatures until person `new` may carry labels, §9 item 12). Closing and converting use existing
ops. No quick-specific state exists.

### 12.10 Trust boundary

| Action | Path | Signature | A dashboard takeover can do it (tier A) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Start an agent with a deposited runner grant | `agent.start` | none | yes |
| Issue a runner grant | click, deposit-only, ≤ `grant_hours` (168 h); or terminal | **yes** | yes when click-to-sign is on |
| Issue agent access with the secret shown once | click, reveal grant sealed to the page (§0.8.6 item 6), local sessions only until 10.5 | **yes** | yes when click-to-sign is on: it can read the secret under its own key |
| Open a shell, attach, type, stop | `term.*`, `run.stop` | none | yes: code execution as the person |
| Create or remove a worktree (force too) | `worktree.*` | none | yes |
| Commit and push records | records child | none | yes (owner, maintainer; only to a URL the export check allows) |
| Turn on dashboard execution, auto push, a private remote | terminal CLI | — | the dashboard has no op for it; a same-UID process can |
| Grant an addon in the workspace | `addon.grant` | **yes** | yes when click-to-sign is on |

- The launched agent has the person's UID: it can read the WSK, the convenience key, ssh keys, the runner's memory
  (every deposited grant), and call the host as column P without `ORCH_GRANT`, including terminals and launches.
  Columns are policy against honest clients, not a boundary against same-UID agents (host §7, §0.8.6 card text).
- The secret is kept out of the HTTP process, the browser and all logs against **passive** disclosure; a takeover can
  make a started agent print it.
- Runs, terminals and worktrees add no reader of the workspace log. The click grant follows the readers condition like
  every click op. A records push adds a reader (D-P2-34). §0.8.6 item 5's rule holds: no addon page can make the
  dashboard call `prepare`, `agent.start`, `term.*` or `run.stop`.
- A person-run Claude or Codex in the dock (`term.open {harness}`) acts as the person, like running it in their own
  terminal (owner FYI).
- Accepted for phase 2 (owner FYI): terminal rendering in the main dashboard origin; an xterm parser bug fed by agent
  output could take over the dashboard. Mitigated by the configuration above; an isolated origin is a phase-3 item.

### 12.11 UI contract for the dashboard (orch-fa)

| Feature | Host ops and items | Dashboard server |
|---|---|---|
| Card line, enablement | `whoami.runner` (`RunnerInfo`, cap `run/1`); `runner.disabled` `detail.missing:"addon"\|"machine"\|"terminals"` | shows the D-P2-31 card line when `enabled` |
| Agents page, dock | `run.sub` first, then `run.list {since}`; keep the higher `rev`; `{t:"gone"}` removes | SSE fan-out like `live.py` (replaces the mockup's `agent.started`/`agent.stopped`) |
| Start dialog | `agent.preview` → show exactly `display`, cwd, env names, grant, warnings, the login-shell line → `agent.start {…, spec}` with idem; `blocked.code` is one of `runner.disabled`, `runner.unavailable`, `launch.claimed`, `launch.no_grant`, `launch.invalid`, `harness.*`, `worktree.*` | core component `SpawnConfirm`; never from an addon frame |
| Dock: person-run shell, Claude, Codex | `term.preview` (shows `display` and the notice "acts as you, not as an agent") → `term.open {…, spec}` with idem | runs as `kind:"shell"` |
| Runner grant | click `prepare {op:"grant", deposit:true}` → `view` (the deposit line) → `sign` → `deposit`; `unknown` → `grant.deposit_status`; fallback hand-off | never receives a secret |
| Terminal | `term.preview`, `term.open`, `term.attach {mode, take, from}`, `attach.cancel`, `run.stop` | §12.6.1 verification, §12.6.6 browser path, §12.6.7 xterm configuration |
| Worktrees | `worktree.list {check}`, `worktree.create`, `worktree.remove {force}` | destructive confirm for `force`; "Open terminal here" = `term.open {cwd:{kind:"worktree", …}}` |
| Records | `records.status` (owners, maintainers) | spawns the records child (one per workspace), shows the export warning, `auto` off switch only |
| Quick tasks | `quick.list {limits}`, existing `new`/`set`/sign paths | limits are a local setting |

Click-eligible versus other ops (G12): click (no typed word since #1198): `grant` with `deposit:true` or `reveal_key`, `addon.grant`. No signature,
dashboard-direct: `agent.start`, `run.stop`, `term.*`, `worktree.*`, the records child. Terminal only: `orch runner
enable`, `orch records remote private`, `orch records auto on`/`--push`, `orch records push --initial`.

**Rules and strings for the dashboard.**

- **Constants in the bundle** (client text, never host text): the D-P2-31 line "Dashboard execution: agents and
  terminals started here run as you. Anything that takes over this dashboard, or any agent it starts, can run
  commands and read your files and keys." (card, Start dialog, terminal header, whenever `runner.enabled`, whatever
  `terminals` says); the deposit line "The secret goes to your orch runner on this machine and is never shown"; the
  export warning "Push publishes every ticket in this workspace to <url>, restricted ones included."; the private
  remote line "orch trusts your word that only you read <url>."; "Output no longer kept"; "Some processes may still be
  running"; "Another tab or device is controlling this terminal" with "Take control"; "Take back"; "the runner changed; try
  again"; "Input paused"; "Input may not have arrived".
- **Idem:** the browser draws one idem per dialog opening (stable across retries), the server forwards it. After a
  timeout the dashboard reads `run.list` and retries with the same idem, never a new one. `launch.changed` reopens the
  dialog with a fresh preview; the dashboard posts exactly the preview's values plus `spec`.
- **Grant states:** `grant_state:"ended"` is not a run state: the agent's next write fails with `grant.expired` and its
  claims lapse (`grant_ended`); the dashboard offers Stop. Exit reasons `spawn_failed`, `lost`, `runner_restarted` are
  errors; `exited` and `stopped` are normal. `grant.list` shows runner grants with label `runner`; the dashboard offers
  "Forget the runner grant on this machine" (`grant.forget`) next to Revoke, and Revoke uses the sign result's `grant`
  in the `unknown` deposit case.
- **Records child:** fixed argv `python -I -m orch.records commit [--push] --workspace <id> --json` or
  `… auto off --workspace <id> --json`; environment `HOME`, `PATH`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `LANG`, and the orch state
  variables only; 60 s limit enforced by the dashboard. Output: one JSON line `{ok:bool, code?:str, message?:str,
  commit?:Sha, pushed?:bool, url?:str}`; exit 0 on success, the catalog exit of `code` otherwise. `url` and `message`
  are rendered through `visible.tsx`.
- **Worktree states:** `missing` and `moved`: offer Remove (the registration only) and Create; `unpinned`: Remove and
  retry Create; `stale_branch`: Remove and Create on the current branch; `dirty:null` shows "unknown";
  `worktree.in_use` offers "Stop the run"; `created_by` through `visible.tsx`.
- **Quick tasks:** one flow with two signatures until §9 item 12 is built, said in the UI.

Limits are in §0.11 (rows marked v1.6) and errors in the v1.6 table of §0.6.

### 12.14 As built in B9 (16 Oct 2026; `orch setup`, Task C: the core side)

`orch setup` (`orch.setup`, dispatched in `cli/main.py` like `runner`) is the **setup process**: refused under `ORCH_GRANT`
or `ORCH_SESSION` and without `/dev/tty`; it runs `host enable` once if no host answers (a dev checkout is refused there),
sets `RLIMIT_CORE=0`, serves `<state>/setup/setup.sock` and stays until the page is finished, cancelled or Ctrl-C.

* **Wire** (`protocol.py`, `server.py`): HTTP/1.1 over the unix socket. Browser routes are `/api/setup/*` only (the dashboard
  proxies them); `/launch`, `/claim`, `/shutdown` have no such prefix. The launch code is single use, 5 min (login links stay 30 s), bound to the
  `setup_id`; it never travels in a URL or an argument: it is a 0600 file `<state>/setup/setup.code` that the dashboard server reads
  and deletes, and claims over the socket together with its own port (`POST /claim {code, port}`); the first claim wins, a
  second one is refused and printed, and the browser is bound to that port (no browser request is answered before it). Every browser call checks `X-Setup-Token`,
  the `Host` header (127.0.0.1 or localhost, the claimed port) and, on a POST, `Origin == http://<Host>`
  and a JSON content type. The session dies on done, cancel or 10 minutes idle, never during a run.
* **Link** (17 Oct): `orch setup` also shows the one-time link (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#launch=...&to=%2Fsetup`) on `/dev/tty` only, never stderr/stdout, and opens the browser through the launcher's 0600 redirect file; the launcher hands the link over an inherited pipe (`--emit-url-fd`), so the code is in no argv or environment. `orch setup --no-browser` shows the link only; over SSH or screen sharing the link is on your terminal, so anyone who sees the screen within 5 minutes could use it first.
* **Profile** (`flow.py`, `facts.py`): a closed schema; refused directories are `$HOME`, its ancestors, `/`, the state and config
  directories, symbolic-link paths and directories holding store files; a registered directory is Finish setup. R5: method
  `click` with `relay` is `click_relay_unsupported`.
* **Secrets** (`steps.Secrets`): generated in core, bytearrays, wiped at the end; reveal once (410), three words confirmed in
  core, five wrong tries end the session and the next one draws new secrets; the one-click path shows the recovery code only.
  **R6 / lockout rule:** the one-click path never shows the passphrase up front, so any failure after the genesis and before
  the conversion is done (signing mismatch, host error, Ctrl-C, internal error) shows it ONCE on the setup terminal before it
  is wiped (`Creator._rescue_passphrase`); a passphrase the person typed in Finish is never shown back. Residual: SIGKILL or
  SIGHUP of the setup process cannot run that code; the key then stays under the unseen passphrase and the recovery code is the way back.
* **Review** (`review.py`): the plan is built in core and rendered with B6 `signcontent`; the digest (R1) covers the canonical
  profile, directory, every planned event (add-on manifest hashes included) and every row. Host-drawn values are "set at
  signing". R2 (no typed word since #1198 C20: the page confirms with a click after the review); R3: the three-word fingerprint is
  also asked on the setup terminal for Finish setup, a runner grant and execution add-ons.
* **Create** (`steps.Creator`): terminal confirm (R3), then genesis through `workspace_init._hosted_bootstrap` (the B5 path,
  shared with `orch setup`), add-on manifests, runner flags, the runner hello wait (R4: no hello, no grant), then the batch.
  `human.prepare` is **one operation per request**, so a dependent chain cannot be prepared in one bundle; the written
  fallback is used: prepare every request, check each with `host.signer.check` and against the review (`check_prepared`,
  R1: every event equals its reviewed rows except the coded volatile fields), and only then ONE
  `PassphraseBackend.unlocked` for `settings.changed`, `addon.granted` x N and `grant.issued` last, each submitted in
  order; the runner grant is handed over in-process with `host.signer.hand_over`. One-click: the convenience flag, then the
  conversion last (R6: retried once; still failing shows the passphrase once on the setup terminal only; Ctrl-C undoes the
  staged copy).
* **Finish** (R7): the facts are read inside `store.locked()` and again at create; a step is done if any history exists.
* **Pinned seams updated:** `PassphraseBackend.generated` (called only from `custody.select.setup_backend`),
  `.unlocked(` also in `setup/steps.py`, `stage_convenience(passphrase=...)` also in `setup/steps.py`: the passphrase is the
  one the setup process generated itself, never text from a browser, argument or file.

### 12.15 The Publish add-on (P5, 18 Oct 2026)

Share files of a ticket with a link, on a server the owner chooses (design: orch-publish `pubsrv`, protocol-v2 §12.1).
The add-on `publish` ships inside orch-core (capability `network`); `addon.grant publish` turns it on, `runner.disabled`
(`detail.missing: "addon"`) while it is off. Nothing leaves the machine without a person's signature.

| Op | Column | What |
|---|---|---|
| `publish.prepare {ref, artifacts[], kind?, days?, views?}` | P; G only on the ticket it claims | copies the named artifacts (by the ticket manifest and digest) into a host-private stage (`<state>/hosts/<ws>/publish/stage/<id>/`, 0700); returns `staged_id` and the exact words a person signs; tags `origin: agent\|person` |
| `publish.share {staged_id}` (through `human.prepare`/`submit`) | person, signed | one `log.added` note on the ticket whose text the host builds from the stage (ticket, who prepared it, link kind, days, views, **server**, **every file with size and hash**, the manifest hash) |
| `publish.send {staged_id}` | P only | builds the same words again from the stage and the signed server setting; requires a person-signed note with exactly these words (the caller's, at most an hour old); registers the workspace if needed, uploads the staged bytes (read, hashed, sent), commits, returns the link **once** and wipes the stage |
| `publish.revoke {share_id}` | P only | `DELETE` on the server, then the record says `revoked` |
| `publish.list {ref?, live?}` | P, G (own claimed ticket) | staged copies and shares (never a link or token); `live` (P) adds the server's state and view counts |
| `publish.discard {staged_id}` | P; G only copies an agent prepared on its claimed ticket | drops a stage |
| `publish.register` | P only | hands the workspace's v2 card and the owner key to the hub (`card_put`); the hub forwards them to orch-publish, which verifies the card and admits the workspace (V3-D36: no direct request) |

* **Server setting** is signed state: `settings.set {set: {publish: {server, share}}}` (owner only; `null` removes it). Both
  are origins (`https://host[:port]`, or `http://127.0.0.1`/`localhost` for this computer), different from each other.
  A change after a signature voids that signature (the words contain both).
* **Token.** `secrets.token_bytes(32)` base64url, 43 characters, made in `publish.send`; the server gets only
  `sha256(token)`. It is held in a 0600 file of the stage until the server commits (so a retry sends the same
  `token_hash`), then wiped with the stage; never in the log, the outcome store, the audit file or an error. The link is
  `<share origin>/s/<share id>#t=<token>` (the token is in the fragment).
* **Registration goes through the hub** (V3-D36, D69). Publishing needs a hub: a workspace without one is local only and
  every `publish.*` network op is refused `hub.not_joined` ("join a hub"); there is no direct path to orch-publish.
  `publish.register` sends `card_put {card, pk_pub}` (the workspace's v2 card and the owner `PK` from the pinned genesis)
  over the hub link; the hub forwards it to orch-publish (`PUT /v2/hub/cards/{ws}`, hub protocol §11), which verifies the
  card itself and applies the admin's pre-bind. The delegation is permanent: the same one is `unchanged`, another is
  `delegation_changed` (reason `conflict`); a card older than the highest admitted is `stale_card` (reason `rejected`).
  The server admin pre-binds the workspace: `orch-publish admin --data DIR owners add OWNER` and `ws allow WS OWNER`;
  `publish.list` carries `workspace` and `owner` so `orch publish setup` can print exactly that when the server answers
  `unknown_workspace`. A join already hands the card to orch-publish, so a pre-bound workspace is admitted at join.
* **No `SignLedger`** is given to the hub-path signer: the server's nonce store refuses a replay, and a file ledger that is
  rewritten on every request and never pruned would only grow.
* **Codes.** `publish.not_configured`, `publish.not_approved`, `publish.changed`, `publish.server_refused`
  (`detail.reason`: `unknown_workspace`, `blocked`, `owner_not_allowed`, `limit`, `conflict`, `clock`, `delegation`,
  `rejected`), `publish.unreachable` (retryable). Rate: 10 per minute per person per kind of request.
* **CLI.** `orch publish setup|register|prepare|share|send|revoke|list|discard` (`orch.cli.publish`). An agent
  (`ORCH_GRANT`) may `prepare`, `list`, `discard`; the rest is `op.not_allowed` here and again in the host. The link is
  written to `/dev/tty` only.
* **Signing class** (#1198 C2, §0.8.6 item 6). `publish.share`, `addon.grant` of `publish` and a
  `settings.set` that touches `publish` are plain clicks after the review (they were terminal-only); the View names both
  servers in words, and the staged copy's own words are the share's review. `orch sign CODE` stays the backup.
  `click/protocol.op_class` still classes `settings.set` by key (`SETTINGS_TERMINAL_KEYS`, now empty) from the
  request's `set` before prepare and from the prepared events at sign time; the sign-time class wins.

## 13. Tier B: agents and add-ons as their own OS user (#1198 H1, #287)

**Status: spec, 24 Oct 2026, not built.** Tasks L1–L13, A1–A4, E1, M1–M3 of #1198 build it. **Owner decisions of 24 Oct
2026** (not reopened): Linux (a headless VPS) first, then Windows, then macOS; One click is on by default only where
isolation is detected (13.7), elsewhere off with a red line; a VPS where the person logs in as `root` gets a normal
person user `orch` from the installer, which runs host, dashboard and keys; dashboard terminals run as the agent user
(a shell as the person stays with SSH); one agent user per person for now; add-ons get slot users (#287) with the
marketplace stream's requirements R-M1 to R-M4 (13.8).

This section is authoritative for tier B. Where it differs from earlier text (D-P2-2, D-P2-5, D-P2-6, D-P2-24, D-P2-27,
D-P2-31, §0.2, §0.8.6, §9 items 10 and 11, §12.4, §12.6, §12.7, H3c), this section wins and the earlier text is
amended to point here. **No migration:** tier A is not a compatibility path. It stays only where tier B does not exist
(no admin step done, Windows, macOS before M1, and the dev sandbox's tests), and the dashboard says so (13.7). On Linux,
once L1–L7 are built, dashboard execution (agent start, terminals) requires tier B.

### 13.1 Principals (Linux)

The host stays the person's UID: **host = the person's OS user**. The threat tier B answers is agents and add-ons, not
the host; a separate host UID stays possible later and nothing here blocks it.

| OS user | Runs | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| the person, e.g. `sev` (= host UID) | host, dashboard server, click signer, CLI, `orch sign` | One-click key, passphrase key, WSK, host state, add-on credentials, the person's checkouts |
| `orch-agent-<user>` (system user, password locked, shell `/bin/bash`) | the runner (system unit), every agent run, every dashboard terminal | its own HOME, its Claude/Codex login, its clones and worktrees, the grants deposited to it |
| `orch-addon-1` … `orch-addon-8` (system users, `nologin`) | one add-on slot runner each and the calls assigned to it | nothing persistent; a per-call work dir |

One agent user per person (not per workspace): a person's agents can read every repository that person shares with
them. Per-workspace agent users are a later option the layout allows. The worker role (H10) is unchanged by this step.
**One naming key.** Every unit instance, writable path and directory of an agent or slot user is keyed by its user
name (`orch-agent-<user>`, `orch-addon-<n>`), never by the person's name or a numeric UID, so the units' `%i`, their
`ReadWritePaths` and the directories always agree. Two things keep the UID: the person's run directory `/run/orch/<person uid>`
(D-P2-2) and the root-owned pins `/etc/orch/pins/<uid>.json` (the `orch.host.pins` format). Where a check starts from a UID (§12.6.1's expected terminal path from `runner.uid`), it maps the UID to
the name with `getpwuid` and requires the root-owned pin of that UID to agree.

Classes are §0.5's: an agent-user connection is class `agent` (column N, or G with a verified grant), never P or C,
so `human.*`, `term.*`, `agent.start`, `grant.deposit` and the control ops are refused by the kernel UID, not by an
environment variable.

### 13.2 The one admin step: `orch-os-setup`

Root is needed once, at install, never at run time: no setuid binary, no capabilities, no root daemon, no polkit rule.
`orch-os-setup` is a short Python program, but **root never runs a file it does not own**: the person's release lives in
the person's home, so it is not what root executes. The installer, as root, downloads the signed release into a root-owned
0700 staging directory, verifies the signed manifest against the bytes there, and runs
`/usr/bin/python3 -I -S <staging>/orch/setup/osinstall.py` (system interpreter, never the release venv, never `-m orch...`).
That step re-checks the staging tree, copies the four stdlib-only setup modules (with the package `__init__` files) and a launcher to the root-owned
`/usr/lib/orch/os-setup/` (`/usr/lib`, not `/usr/local`: Debian's `/usr/local` can be group-writable), and re-hashes the copy
against the source. The launcher `/usr/lib/orch/os-setup/orch-os-setup` has the shebang `#!/usr/bin/python3 -IS` (one argument: Linux does not split shebang arguments); before it
imports anything of orch it checks that the interpreter, the standard library and the whole copy (and every directory above
them) are root's and not writable by group or other, and afterwards that every loaded orch module came from the copy. The
installer runs it when it is root (most VPSs); otherwise setup shows one line to copy,
`sudo /usr/lib/orch/os-setup/orch-os-setup --person <user> --release <release>`, with a "Check again" button (the installer
has put the copy there; the release path is validated: absolute, plain characters, root-owned). It computes a plan from OS
facts, prints it, applies it (`--dry-run` prints the exact actions), and may run again: it repairs, it never widens. It uses
fixed absolute binaries. Directories below an agent-owned one are only ever opened file-descriptor-relative with
`O_NOFOLLOW` (never by path), so a symlink planted by the agent is refused. The agent's runner is started only after root
has recorded the sudo/SSH verdict; a re-run whose verdict fails stops the runner and drops the verdict from the pin.

1. **Users.** `useradd --system --user-group --home-dir /var/lib/orch/agents/orch-agent-<user>/home --create-home --shell
   /bin/bash orch-agent-<user>`, password locked; `orch-addon-1..8` with `/usr/sbin/nologin` and home
   `/var/lib/orch/addons/orch-addon-<n>`. A pre-existing user of one of these names without orch's pin is refused, never adopted.
2. **Privileged groups refused.** If an agent or slot user is in `sudo`, `wheel`, `admin`, `adm`, `docker`, `lxd`,
   `libvirt`, `disk` or `shadow` (each is root or close to it), the helper refuses. The host checks again at every
   start (13.6).
3. **Pins.** Root-owned `/etc/orch/pins/<uid>.json`: `{"class":"agent"|"addon","host_uid":…,"workspaces":"*"}`
   (the `orch.host.pins` format; class `addon` is new). A pinned UID is never a person.
4. **Run directories** (`/etc/tmpfiles.d/orch.conf`):
   - `d /run/orch 0755 root root`;
   - `d /run/orch/<person uid> 2750 <person> orch-agent-<user>`: setgid, so every socket the host creates inside
     carries the agent's group without the person joining it; the host `chmod`s each socket it shares to 0660. The
     control directory inside stays 0700;
   - `d /run/orch/agents/orch-agent-<user> 0750 orch-agent-<user> orch-agent-<user>` plus the ACL `u:<person>:rwx`,
     default `u:<person>:rw`, so the dashboard (the person) can reach the runner's terminal socket without joining any
     group (a group change needs a re-login of the person's systemd user manager).
5. **Agent tree.** `/var/lib/orch/agents/orch-agent-<user>/{home,state,repos}`, owned by the agent, 0700, except `repos` 0750
   with the default ACL `d:u:<person>:rX` (the host reads clones through `orch.gitread`).
6. **Person-side sharing**, set **as the person** by the CLI right after (no root needed for one's own files):
   `u:<agent>:x` on each ancestor of the release, the interpreter and each workspace repository inside the person's
   home; `u:<agent>:rX` plus a default ACL on the release tree and on `<repo>/.git` only. Each ACL is read back and
   verified.
7. **Units.** `orch-runner@.service` (instance = the person) and `orch-addon@.service` (instance = the slot number),
   the runner enabled and started (add-on slot units are written but enabled by L3): `User=orch-agent-%i` (the instance is the bare person name, e.g. `orch-runner@sev`, so no instance such as `root` can ever run as root; slots: `orch-addon@<n>` with `User=orch-addon-%i`), `Delegate=yes` (per-run cgroups, D-P2-29), `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `PrivateTmp=yes`,
   `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome=read-only`, `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/orch/agents/orch-agent-%i /run/orch/agents/orch-agent-%i`,
   `RestrictSUIDSGID=yes`, `TasksMax=`, `MemoryMax=` (agent: 80 % of RAM by default; D-P2-29's "no limits in phase 2"
   was a tier-A limit), plus `ProtectProc=invisible`, `ProtectKernelTunables/Modules/Logs`, `ProtectClock`,
   `ProtectHostname`, `LockPersonality`, `RestrictRealtime` and `SystemCallArchitectures=native` (`ProtectControlGroups` stays
   off: `Delegate=yes` needs a writable cgroup tree). `ReadWritePaths` is the agent's own tree (`home` for its
   Claude/Codex login, `state`, `repos`) and its run directory; the state directory is the agent's, never the person's.
   `ExecStart` is the person's `<release>/current/bin/orch-runner` (the release build writes it next to `orch-host`).
   **Start check:** `ExecStartPre=+/usr/bin/python3 -I -S /usr/lib/orch/os-setup/orch-os-setup --recheck %i` runs as root
   (the `+` prefix) from the trusted copy, never from the release, before every start, including every `Restart=always`
   restart (`RestartSec=2`; the start limit then holds a unit that keeps failing). It asks `sudo -l -U` and `sshd -T`
   again (authoritative, so LDAP and sssd are covered), runs setup's user, group and pin checks, and exits non-zero if
   any answer changed: it drops the verdict from the pin (the host answers broken) and systemd refuses the start. It
   never calls `systemctl` (stopping a unit from its own start job would wait on itself). When every answer still holds
   it refreshes the pin's stat signatures, so a harmless edit elsewhere in `/etc/ssh` does not leave the host saying
   "policy changed" until the next setup run. On a new release the host sends `runner.restart` (it notices at
   `runner.hello` that the runner loaded another release, once per release); the runner exits when it has no live runs
   (`force`: at once) and `Restart=always` starts the new code, so updates need no root. The person's CLI only reads the
   unit (`is-active`, `show`); it never installs, starts or stops it.
8. **Report.** It prints what it did. A root login: the installer creates the person user `orch` first and the tunnel
   line uses it. Running the dashboard as root would still separate agents, but a dashboard takeover would then be a
   takeover of the server.

### 13.3 Run directory and sockets (amends D-P2-2, D-P2-6, §0.2, §12.6.1)

- `<run>` = `/run/orch/<person uid>`, mode 2750, owner the person, group `orch-agent-<user>` (setgid). This replaces,
  for Linux tier B, D-P2-6's mode 0711 and per-workspace `orch-<ws>` groups (they stay the later per-workspace option).
  The ancestor rules of D-P2-6 apply; a root-owned `/run/orch` 0755 is the helper-made parent. **Invariant:** inside
  `<run>` only the shared sockets (and the directories leading to them) are group-accessible; every other file (pid
  files, launch codes, state) is 0600 and every other directory 0700. L4 teaches the transport's ancestor and ACL
  checks to accept the setgid bit and group `r-x` on `<run>` and nothing wider.
- Workspace sockets `<run>/<ws>/host.sock` and the runner socket `<run>/runner/host.sock`: owner the person, group the
  agent's (inherited), socket 0660. The control socket directory stays 0700: `host.*` stay person-only.
- The runner connects as before (D-P2-24): peer UID = the registered runner UID, bound to the unit's `MainPID` read over
  systemd's D-Bus (readable by any user); the runner checks that its peer is the host UID.
- The terminal socket moves to `/run/orch/agents/orch-agent-<user>/term.sock` (agent-owned directory with the person's ACL,
  socket 0660). §12.6.1's checks apply with that path: the directory owned by the runner UID, no write for others
  except the person's ACL entry, peer UID and PID equal the runner's.
- The agent's `orch` CLI finds the host by `ORCH_HOST_RUN_DIR=/run/orch/<person uid>` from the runner's environment.
- No abstract Unix sockets on the person's side (everyone can reach those); kept as a tested invariant.

### 13.4 Files, and the agent's own clone

| Thing | Owner, mode | Agent can |
|---|---|---|
| One-click key `<state>/person/<ws>/devices/<d>.key` | person, 0600 in 0700 dirs | nothing |
| passphrase key, WSK, host state, add-on credentials, all of `<state>/` | person, 0700/0600 | nothing |
| person's `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` | person | nothing if 0700/0600; **an other-readable file in a home the agent may traverse is readable** (the doctor lists and fixes these, L13) |
| person's working tree (incl. untracked `.env`) | person | nothing |
| person's `<repo>/.git` | person + ACL `u:agent:rX` | read (fetch) |
| workspace store `<root>/.orch/` | person | nothing directly; only through the host socket |
| agent clone `/var/lib/orch/agents/orch-agent-<user>/repos/<ws8>/<name>/` and its worktrees | agent + default ACL `u:person:rX` | everything |
| release and interpreter | person + ACL `u:agent:rX` | read, execute |

**Worktrees are worktrees of a clone the agent owns** (amends §12.7). A `git worktree add` into the person's
repository would put the agent's metadata, refs and objects into the person's `.git`; across UIDs that needs a
writable `.git`, and a writable `.git` lets the agent plant `config` or hooks that the person's next `git` runs as the
person, a full escape. So there is one clone per (agent user, repository), fetched as the agent from the person's
`.git`, and per-ticket worktrees of that clone. `safe.directory` is passed on the command line
(`-c safe.directory=<exact path>`), never written to a file and never `*`. The gitsafe owner rule becomes "owned by the
pinned person UID" for the fetch source and "owned by me" for the clone. The way back is unchanged in kind: `diff`,
`tree.check` and landing read the agent's clone through `orch.gitread` as the host (the host runs `tree.check` itself,
as in tier A; the worker split of H10 is not required for tier B). **Condition:** the host reads an agent-owned tree
only through the `orch.gitread` child with its limits, opened from the pinned directory with `O_NOFOLLOW`, objects by
id; no git process ever runs there (#565), landing imports objects into the host's bare
repository (`land/git.py`). The person's own `git` refuses the agent's clone (dubious ownership); the doctor warns on
`safe.directory=*`. A ticket without a codebase works in a work folder inside the agent's tree (L6 fixes the path),
not in the person's project root (§12.4.4), which the agent cannot write. The runner creates and writes it; the host
only reads it (`orch.gitread`, or fd-relative `O_NOFOLLOW` reads) and **never writes or deletes anything inside an
agent-owned tree** (symlink races).

**The store and the guard.** The agent reaches `.orch/` only through the host socket. Direct mode (D-P2-18) under an
agent UID refuses with a plain message ("this workspace is served by its host"), not with `EACCES` (L7). The plugin's
hooks (`orch instructions hook …`) run as the agent through the socket; `instructions.hook` must accept the agent
class (today it is P-only and works because a tier-A agent is person class).

### 13.5 Runner, environment, terminals, sign-in (amends D-P2-24, D-P2-27, D-P2-31, §12.4.3, §12.6)

- **The runner is the agent user** (one system unit per agent user, 13.2 item 7), so it starts runs through the existing
  trampoline (`runner/exec.py`) without any UID change. Grants deposited to it are bound to the runner UID (§9 item 11).
- **Environment.** The run's environment comes from the runner's own (the `ENV_FROM_RUNNER` allow-list): `HOME` is the
  agent's; `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and the person's API keys and tokens do not exist there. Agents push only through landing or
  a deploy key of their own. Docker through the person's daemon is refused (the `docker` group is root); rootless
  podman as the agent is fine.
- **Terminals run as the agent user**, never as the person; there is no "shell as me" in the dashboard (a shell as the
  person stays with SSH). **Card line** in tier B (terminal header, Start dialog, workspace card), replacing D-P2-31's
  line there: **"This terminal runs as orch-agent-<user>. It cannot read your keys."** D-P2-31's line ("…run as you…")
  stays only where tier B is not active. D-P2-27's risk sentence for the runner grant stays (a dashboard takeover can
  still give agents standing authority).
- **Agent sign-in.** Agents log in to Claude Code and Codex once, as themselves, in an agent terminal ("Sign in your
  agents": `claude` login, `codex login --device-auth` on a headless VPS), or with a pasted token or API key that
  reaches the runner sealed and is written into the agent's own HOME 0600 (L10). They never use the person's login,
  SSH key or GitHub token. The Claude trust file is written into the agent's HOME (unchanged code, different HOME).

### 13.6 `isolation.detect()` (L11)

Isolation is read from OS facts on every call (cached at most 60 s, with the ancestor checks of D-P2-6), never from a
flag, a setting or a file the person's UID could write. It answers per role `isolated`, `same_user` or `broken`, with the
first failed fact named.

- **Agents `isolated`** only if all hold: the runner's peer UID ≠ the person UID; a root-owned pin
  `/etc/orch/pins/<uid>.json` with class `agent` and this `host_uid`; the agent user in none of the privileged groups of
  13.2 item 2 (from the group database, not the user's claim); the runner unit active with `User=` that UID (D-Bus);
  `<run>`, the control directory and the person's `<state>` with the owners and modes of 13.2–13.4 and no ACL entry for
  the agent on `<state>` or the key files.
- **Add-ons `isolated`** only if, for the slot in question: a root-owned pin with class `addon`; slot UID ≠ person UID
  and ≠ any agent UID; not in a privileged group; `orch-addon@<n>` active with that `User=`; the add-on's package and
  environment readable by that slot and **not readable by any other slot** (ACL read back), and not writable by the slot
  (R-M2).
- **`same_user`**: no agent or slot users (tier A). **`broken`**: users exist but a fact fails; the doctor names it.
  The failed facts split by cause:
  - **exposure facts** (an agent could reach the key or act as the person): the agent or slot user in a privileged
    group; an ACL entry for it on `<state>` or a key file; a missing or foreign pin; the runner's peer UID is the
    person's; `<run>` or the control directory wider than 13.3. These **pause click signing** (13.7) and keep the
    marketplace gate closed;
  - **availability facts** (nothing is exposed, something is down): the runner or slot unit not active. One click
    stays on, with the red line and the doctor; the marketplace gate stays closed for an inactive slot.
- Used by: the One-click default (13.7), the dashboard's status line ("Agents run as their own user" or the red line),
  the marketplace gate (13.8, #929) and setup's "Check again".

### 13.7 One click in tier B (reverses §9 item 11 "click-to-sign ends after migration")

- **One click is allowed in tier B.** With host = person, the click signer keeps running as the person next to the
  dashboard (§0.8.6 item 5); the signer needs no change. Agents cannot read the key file and cannot reach the signer
  (a `socketpair` child of the dashboard server, no path to connect to).
- **Default.** On by default where `isolation.detect()` says agents are `isolated`. Off by default elsewhere (no admin
  step, Windows, macOS before M1, `broken`): turning it on is one click after the red line **"Agents run as you.
  Anything an agent runs can sign with One click and read your files."** (plus the step-up of §0.8.6 10.5 on a remote session).
  If isolation later turns `broken` while One click is on: an **exposure fact** (13.6) **pauses click signing**. The
  signer refuses each sign with the failed fact named; custody, the key and the person's setting do not change, and
  signing resumes by itself once the check passes again. An **availability fact** leaves One click on, with the red line
  and the doctor. Pausing rather than switching off means an agent that breaks something (for example kills its own
  runner) gains no lever over the person's custody; `orch sign CODE` in the terminal keeps working throughout.
- **§0.8.6 item 3a works in tier B.** The host-state flag file is the person's (host = person), so the dashboard's custody
  switch is offered in both tiers.
- **The dashboard port (L8, Linux).** The dashboard server drops loopback TCP connections whose socket owner UID
  (`sock_diag` or `/proc/net/tcp{,6}`) is not the person. The SSH tunnel's forwarding runs as the person, so the VPS path
  keeps working; an agent does not even reach the login. macOS has no equivalent; there the bearer remains the gate.
- Memory: another UID cannot `ptrace` the person's processes or read their `/proc/<pid>/environ` or `mem`. `argv` is
  world-readable unless `/proc` is mounted `hidepid=invisible` (doctor hint), so secrets stay out of `argv` (tested
  invariant).

### 13.8 Add-ons under slot users (#287)

- **Slots, not per-install users.** Making a user needs root; an install must not. The helper makes
  `orch-addon-1..8` and their units once. Granting a community add-on assigns a free slot (host state, person-owned) and
  sets `u:orch-addon-<n>:rX` on that add-on's package and G4 environment only. No free slot: refused with "run setup
  again to add slots".
- **Call path.** The slot runner connects to `<run>/addon/host.sock` (one connection per slot UID, from the unit's
  `MainPID`, like the runner). The host sends `{call, package path, request}`; the slot runs the existing
  `addons/runner.call` (G4's environment verify inside, closed environment, a per-call work dir in its own home, a cgroup
  per call so a `setsid` escape is killed too).
- **Built-in and official add-ons** may keep running as today or move to a shared slot later; tier B does not block
  either.
- **R-M1, check order (A4).** Lifting `market.community_unisolated` (#929) never bypasses hub policy: on a hub-joined
  workspace the marketplace spec's D14/G7 decide first which marketplaces are allowed, then isolation. `isolation.detect()` only removes the
  isolation refusal. A4's T0 includes a hub refusal with isolation detected: it stays refused.
- **R-M2, the environment is read-only for the slot (A2, checked in A1).** G4 environments are built and verified by the
  host user (`host/addonenv.py`, the envtree stamp). The slot can read the env and its stamp but not write them
  (person-owned, no write ACL), so an add-on cannot defeat the runtime verify. A2 reads the ACL back and fails on any
  write bit for the slot; A1 keeps `envtree.verify` inside the call.
- **R-M3, the credential stays host-owned (A3).** The credential file (`<state>/hosts/<ws>/addons/<name>/credential`,
  0600, host user) stays host-owned with #1179's fd-relative store; the host passes it on stdin per call. The slot never
  gets a path or a descriptor to it. Marketplace spec §15.1's tier-A credential limit closes.
- **R-M4, `{python}` under the slot (A2, tested in A1).** G4's `{python}` line (`-B -s -S`, `PYTHONPATH` from an empty
  environment) must work as the slot: the interpreter and its stdlib, the package copy and the env are readable and the
  interpreter executable by the slot (ACL `rX`, set and read back by A2). A1's T0 runs a `{python}` add-on as the slot.

### 13.9 Threat model

| Attacker | Tier A (no isolation) | Tier B |
|---|---|---|
| **Agent** (prompt-injected or malicious) | Runs as the person: reads the One-click key and signs anything it allows; reads SSH keys, tokens and every file; calls every person and control op except signing without a key (§7); drives the dashboard locally; writes the store files directly | Column G ops of its grant; reads the shared repositories' `.git` and its own files; its own Claude/Codex credentials (it can leak those: give it a separate key with a spend limit); the network; the other runs of the same agent user (no per-run isolation). **Cannot** read or use the keys, reach the signer or (Linux) the dashboard port, call human or control ops, write the store, write the person's files, or push with the person's credentials |
| **Paths from an agent to the person** that tier B leaves | — | (a) content it writes that the dashboard renders (ticket text, artifacts, terminal output): an XSS there is an escalation, so strict CSP and safe rendering are now the main boundary; (b) social engineering in what the person approves (the review shows what is signed; hub steps need the backup key); (c) the person running the agent's code as themselves (`npm install`, tests); (d) kernel or setup bugs (an unpatched kernel; an agent in a privileged group, refused by the helper and the host) |
| **Compromised dashboard** (XSS, stolen bearer, malicious dependency of the server) | Everything | Unchanged: it runs as the person, so it can click-sign everything One click covers and start agents. Hub ops still need the backup key; secrets travel sealed. Shrunk by idle auto-off, the short bearer and passkey step-up (§0.8.6 item 10), the key at rest (H3) and L8 (an agent can no longer be the local attacker that takes it over) |
| **Malicious add-on** (community, after #287) | Runs as the person: everything; therefore community marketplaces are refused (`market.community_unisolated`) | Its slot UID only: its env (read-only), its per-call work dir, its credential for one call (stdin), the network if granted. Not the keys, not agents' files, not other add-ons' credentials or envs |
| **Another local user** | As §0.8.6 item 8 | Same; plus L8 drops their loopback connections to the dashboard on Linux |
| **Root** | Out of scope | Out of scope |

**Sudo and SSH policy check, and its limit (L2/L11).** The root-owned pin records the verdict of `sudo -l -U` and
`sshd -T` taken at setup, plus the stat signature of each policy file. The unprivileged host compares signatures on
every `detect()`. Where the person cannot search a policy folder (Ubuntu and RHEL: `/etc/sudoers.d` is 0750 root), only
the folder's own signature is recorded: an entry added, removed or renamed is seen, but an **in-place edit of an existing
file inside that folder is not**, because only root can stat it (the edit needs root as well, so this sits inside the
"Root: out of scope" row). A folder the person can list but not search refuses with "is new" for any entry that was not
recorded; that fails closed and is accepted. A recorded entry the host cannot stat (a symlink to a root-only target)
reads as changed. **Closed by L3:** the runner unit's `ExecStartPre=+… --recheck %i` (13.2 item 7) asks `sudo -l -U` and
`sshd -T` again at each runner start as root, refuses the start if an answer changed and rewrites the pin without a
verdict. It runs at start, not continuously: a rule added while the runner runs is caught at its next start (or setup
rerun), and the host's signature comparison covers the time in between.

**What tier A honestly loses.** Without isolation, anything an agent runs can sign with One click and read every file
of the person, including SSH keys and tokens; the column split of §0.5 is policy, not a boundary; community add-ons
stay refused. The dashboard shows the red line "Agents run as you" and One click is off by default. An unprivileged
bubblewrap sandbox could hide paths from a same-user agent, but it is weaker (same UID, shared loopback; Ubuntu 24.04
restricts unprivileged user namespaces) and is not part of this plan.

### 13.10 Windows (after the Windows host)

Today there is no host, runner or click signer on Windows (D-P2-38): agents a person starts there run as the person,
can use the One-click key and read every file of the person. The dashboard says so and One click is off by default.
**Planned** (design first, with the Windows host port): a local standard account `orch-agent` created by the installer
(one UAC prompt), never in Administrators; the runner as a Windows service under that account (or a virtual service
account `NT SERVICE\orch-runner`); host named pipes with an explicit DACL and the client token's SID checked; the
dashboard's loopback peer check by owning PID (`GetExtendedTcpTable`) to token SID; keys in the person's
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` (the profile ACL excludes other standard users) plus DPAPI user scope (H3); repository sharing with
`icacls`; ConPTY terminals as the agent account. Not protected even then: an administrator account, and anything the
person runs as themselves.

### 13.11 macOS (last, M1–M3)

**Until M1:** tier A, with the same red line and One click off by default. **Planned:** a hidden role user
(`sysadminctl -addUser orch-agent-<user>`, `IsHidden`), not in `admin` or `staff`; the runner as a LaunchDaemon with
`UserName`; run directory `/Users/Shared/orch/run/<uid>` (H3c; BSD semantics give new files the directory's group, so no
setgid is needed); ACLs with `chmod +a`; one admin password prompt at install. The person's login keychain is in their
0700 `~/Library`, out of the agent's reach. **What is not protected or does not work:** there is no kernel peer check
for loopback TCP, so an agent can reach the dashboard's login and only the bearer stops it; repositories under
`~/Documents`, `~/Desktop` or `~/Downloads` are TCC-protected and a daemon user gets no prompt (setup says "keep code
outside these folders"); Claude Code under a daemon user has no unlocked keychain and uses `claude setup-token` or an API
key in the agent's own file. Touch ID and the keychain stay extras for the person's key. This replaces H3c's agent-user
part; H3c's per-workspace groups and worker daemon stay later options.

### 13.12 Build tasks

L1 setup plan (pure) → L2 apply and the root-owned launcher `/usr/lib/orch/os-setup/orch-os-setup`; L3 runner as system unit; L4 run directory and sockets; L5
person-side ACLs; L6 agent clone and worktrees; L7 agent CLI (served mode only, `instructions.hook`, environment); L8
dashboard peer-UID check; L9 terminals as the agent; L10 agent sign-in; L11 `isolation.detect()`; L12 the setup step;
L13 doctor; A1–A4 slots, ACLs, credentials per call, #929; E1 e2e `vps-agent-uid` on the dev VPS; M1–M3 macOS. Real
cross-UID tests run in a CI job with root (`needs_root`, `tests/osusers/`); locally they skip.
